findings.right_value: if Text.Contains([Item], ":") then Text.Trim(Text.AfterDelimiter([Item], ":")) else Text.Trim([Item])
findings.consequence: Only one side applies Text.Trim. The same NetSuite value therefore produces two different key strings, so rows that should join do not, and the same item can appear twice in a combined view.
findings.recommendation: Normalise the key once, in the canonical layer, and never per query.

findings.subject: output column "Available"
findings.consequence: Both queries emit a column called "Available" from the same export, but they aggregate different source columns. Any comparison, join or roll-up across the two is comparing different measures under one name — and nothing in either workbook shows that.
findings.recommendation: Define this measure once in the canonical layer and give each variant a distinct, honest name.

findings.subject: Csv.Document option QuoteStyle
findings.consequence: QuoteStyle.None ignores CSV quoting, so any field containing a comma splits across columns and silently shifts every value after it on that row. The two queries are reading the same bytes into different tables.
findings.recommendation: Read the export once, with QuoteStyle.Csv, and reuse it.
